name: Uruguay
reused_from: SE/NO dual pattern (kernel Dual idea, written as Cat. I/II)
sources_official_secondary: BPC 2025 = $ 6.576 from DGI's 'Base de Prestaciones y Contribuciones (BPC)' table (Decreto 05/025 behind IMPO login)

validation.referee: statute's own printed tables and thresholds (#guard / decide)

unsupported: aguinaldo (SAC) and salario vacacional taxed at a proportional rate (art. 36 inc. 2, 37 last inc.) not separated: all wages enter the scale
montepio 15 % applied without the cap of Ley 20.130 art. 22 ($ 215.179 at the law's base date, indexed: 2025 value not reached); FRL contribution and FONASA spouse surcharge not modelled
nucleo familiar elections (art. 37 B/C) not modelled; child deduction shared equally between two parents (art. 38: shared in equal parts when the parents agree)
pensions: taxed by the IASS (Ley 18.314), not by the IRPF: not modelled
interest: art. 26 A rates depend on currency and term (0,5 % to 12 %); 12 % ('restantes rentas') applied
rent: art. 26 B 12 % on gross rent (deductible costs and the art. 27 J exemption below 40 BPC not modelled)
selfEmployment: art. 34 30 % deduction applied; IRAE option and BPS contributions of non-dependents not modelled

scale.source: IRPF Titulo 7 arts. 37 A and 38: the 180 BPC threshold at BPC $ 6.576 (Decreto 05/025, DGI table)

headline: Uruguay 2025 IRPF from IMPO's Titulo 7: BPC 6.576 scale 0-36 %, a statute-visible notch of about $ 13.849 at 180 BPC (credit rate 14 % -> 8 %), FONASA notch at 2,5 BPC a month.
